business_scope: Maize/corn market pricing cycles, industrial feed/starch demand, moisture percentage discounting rules, and storage risk management.

crop_business_factors.details: Maize prices typically dip immediately following the Kharif harvest window (Oct-Nov) due to high, synchronized market arrivals across major producing states.
A vast majority of maize is consumed by the poultry feed industry, starch manufacturers, and ethanol plants, tying baseline prices directly to industrial output demand.

common_risks.details: Mandi buyers apply steep price deductions or reject grain outright if moisture content exceeds the 14% threshold, leading to severe financial loss.

market_factors.details: Prices tend to recover gradually toward the summer months (April-June), rewarding farmers who invest in mechanical drying and secure dry storage.

revenue_factors: Total dry grain volume sold to industrial buyers or feedmills
cost_revenue_factors.important_rule: Corn profitability depends heavily on drying grain below safe moisture thresholds to avoid mandi penalties and capturing post-harvest price recoveries.

strengths: Robust structural demand from expanding poultry and ethanol blending sectors.
weaknesses: High vulnerability to fungal toxins (aflatoxins) if improperly dried.
opportunities: Establishing direct contract-farming tie-ups with industrial feed processors.
threats: Unseasonal rains during harvest causing widespread grain moisture damage.

things_to_monitor: Poultry feed industry consumption rates and regional price trends
Grain moisture percentage readings prior to sale or storage
Local APMC arrival volumes during peak Kharif months
